definition: The project name of the whole product, made of one Station, one or more Pods and a Power Management Unit.
The marketing name of the cocktail-maker.
The central unit with the touch display that runs the host application and starts every exchange with the Pods.
A self-contained dispensing unit with its own controller that weighs and pours ingredients when the Station commands it.
The unique name of a Pod, which the Pod reports and the Station uses to address it.
The embedded controller board of a Pod that drives its actuators and reads its load cells.
The Raspberry Pi inside the Station that runs the host application.
The part of the machine that turns the mains voltage into the low DC voltages for the Station and the Pods.
The external mains supply that powers the machine.
The bottles of spirits, juices and syrups that an Operator puts into the machine.
The person who orders and receives a drink and needs no technical knowledge.
The person who refills, cleans and calibrates the machine.
The Station screens where a Guest picks a recipe and a glass.
The PIN-protected part of the Station UI where an Operator maintains and calibrates the machine.
A drink component with a type and a boost category, which recipes use and dispensers hold.
A named list of dispense and manual steps for one drink, with a nominal serving volume.
The drink volume that the amounts of a recipe refer to, which the Station scales to the chosen glass.
An adjustment that makes a drink stronger or weaker by shifting volume between its ingredients at the same total volume.
A glass type with common and active volumes that a Guest can choose for a drink.
The part of a Pod that delivers one ingredient, either a pump or a valve.
A dispenser that moves liquid with a stepper motor.
A dispenser with a servo-driven pinch valve that opens and closes a flow.
The sensor of a Pod that weighs a bottle or a glass.
The measurement that ties a load cell reading or a dispenser run to a real amount, which the Pod keeps across power cycles.
Taking the current load on a load cell as its zero point.
The amount of liquid left in the bottle of a dispenser.
To pour a given volume of one ingredient through one dispenser.
One request from the Station and the Pod's answer to it, linked by an ID in the protocol and never shown to a Guest.
